_manifest_sync_precondition: MANDATORY, every registration, checked at registration time and after every subsequent edit to this file: before calling `scope-gate ready` for the first time, and again after any edit to this authored contract, diff this file against the runtime manifest at .autopilot/state/backlog-rows-2026-08-27--v5/manifest.json and print the result -- a printed diff, not an assurance that they match. Compare by EXCLUSION, not by an enumerated include-list: `jq 'walk(if type == "object" then with_entries(select(.key | test("^_") or . == "manifest_schema_version" or . == "review_gate_version" | not)) else . end) | .security_review.reason = null'` on both files, then compare the two results directly. Two things this exact form fixes over a naive version: `walk()` strips underscore-prefixed keys recursively at every nesting depth, not just the top level (a bare `with_entries` misses nested fields like `verification._note`, measured as a real false-negative); nulling `security_review.reason` specifically removes the one non-underscore-prefixed field that is prose (an explanatory rationale, rewritten across rounds) rather than a gate-bound term -- comparing it whole produces a false MISMATCH even when the actual term (`security_review.required`) hasn't changed. An include-list needs advance knowledge of every field the gate reads -- a set that can grow whenever the kit adds one; the exclude-list only needs to know which fields the gate does NOT read, a much smaller and more stable set. The runtime manifest is hash-locked at registration and is what the gate actually obeys; this file is what a human or agent actually reads and edits. Nothing enforces that they agree except this check.
